what.capability: One record per job, from the first conversation to cash received
what.detail: An opportunity becomes the project without retyping anything. The internal ID and the Finance job code live on the same record.

what.capability: A next action with an owner, a due date and what "done" means
what.detail: Every queue item says why it is there, who owns it and when it is due.
Each check says what it means, what is missing or waiting, who does the next step (by name when the project names someone), where, and what completes it. It offers only what your role may do.

what.capability: Next steps suggested after each save
what.detail: When a save completes a check, the next eligible steps appear with an owner, a dated estimate and how it was worked out. A suggestion assigns nothing until someone saves it.

what.capability: Handoffs as tasks with a brief and a review
what.detail: Account assigns Design and Studio work with a brief link and a due date; the output comes back for review.
Each session is recorded with its project, room, planned and actual times, status and assignee. They are records, not reservations.

what.capability: Cost and scope changes proposed with evidence, approved by Finance
what.detail: The governed scenario shows the effect first. Approval saves a new revision and its audit event in one transaction; the earlier figure stays explainable.
Who may change what is enforced by the database itself, not by hidden buttons. Nobody can give themselves Finance authority.
A line without an amount keeps its project out of margin and is listed, never counted as 0.

what.capability: Contract, acceptance and cash kept apart
what.detail: Commercial stage, delivery, financial verification and payment are four separate states.

what.capability: Governed reports that explain their numbers
what.detail: Every figure comes from one set of definitions; "Why this number?" shows the definition, date basis, filters, freshness and records.

what.capability: Bring a sheet in with one template
what.detail: The sheet is filled in on one template and imported as a CSV file. Rows are matched on the sheet's own IDs, so importing the same sheet twice changes nothing.

what.capability: Holistics reports kept with CRM records
what.detail: Links to reports built in Holistics, next to the client or project they are about. This opens Holistics; it does not move data.

what.capability: A guided walkthrough of one project's whole lifecycle
what.detail: On the real screens, with a new sample project and the demo personas: BD, Account and Finance each do their part, in turn.

tools.name: Spreadsheets
tools.text: Fill in one import template and bring it in as a CSV file. Rows are matched on the sheet's own IDs, so importing it again changes nothing.

tools.name: Notes and documents
tools.text: They stay where they are. Job 360 keeps a link to each document, with its type and who added it.

tools.name: Holistics
tools.text: Reports built in Holistics are linked from the client or project they are about. Each one opens in Holistics.

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.text: Every record and every permission check lives in one PostgreSQL database; the screens cannot get round it.

tools.name: Anfra
tools.text: Gross profit, margin, acceptance and cash come from one set of definitions, and each figure can explain itself.

faq.q: Is any of this real customer data?
faq.a: No. The records, screenshots and guide use synthetic examples.

faq.q: What has been measured so far?
faq.a: This example makes no claim about customer outcomes.

faq.q: Who can change a money figure?
faq.a: Account proposes a change with a reason and evidence; Finance approves or rejects it, never its own. The database enforces this, not the screens, and the earlier figure stays explainable.

faq.q: Does it replace the accounting package or the collaboration tools?
faq.a: No. It keeps one record per job and the approvals around its money, next to the tools the teams use today. A sheet comes in as a CSV file, on one import template.

faq.q: What do I need to run it?
faq.a: Node.js, PostgreSQL through Docker, and Anfra 0.8.0. The README describes local setup.

faq.q: How do I explore the demo?
faq.a: Choose a demo persona and start the guided walkthrough from the top bar.
